Column A

Column A in the Excel template is not written to the w2_Algae_Toxin.csv input file. It is used only for descriptive labels in the spreadsheet.

docs.title: Dissolved Gas Added to Turbine Input File
docs.text:
This file is a time series file of Julian day and a fraction multiplied by the incoming turbine dissolved oxygen. This file is assumed to be a step function input. The file is either for a spillway (w2_spX_DO.csv, where X is the spillway number) or for a gate (w2_gtX_DO.csv, where X is the gate number).

The fraction will usually be greater than or equal to 1.0. If it is 1.0, the inflow oxygen is unchanged. If it is 1.1, the inflow oxygen is increased by 10%. Other parameters for the spillway or gate dictate whether the outflow oxygen is limited or not by 100% saturation.

The file has the following format: the first 3 lines are ignored and then there is a time series of Julian day and fraction.

Field Variable Description 1 JDAY Julian day 2 FRAC Fraction multiplied by incoming dissolved oxygen (DO)

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
Input fraction for gate1
Dynamic turbine venting
JDAY,FRAC
1,1
210.5,1.1
300,1
365,1

docs.title: Automatic Port Selection
docs.text:
The CE-QUAL-W2 model reads the file w2_selective.npt if the SELECTC control is set to ON or USGS in the control file (w2_con.npt or w2_con.csv). This input file allows the model user to:

  1. Automatically choose a withdrawal port elevation based on meeting required temperature targets
  2. Print temperature of individual outlets rather than combining them together
  3. Print the volume of the reservoir at specified temperature targets

Note

If DYNSTRUC is set to ON in the control file, the port selection in this file is ignored when there is not an active rule. When a rule is inactive, the input file of elevations (when DYNSTRUC=ON) will control the centerline of the structure.

docs.title: SELECTC = ON
docs.text: When SELECTC='ON', the input file is named w2_selective.npt. There are three independent sections: (1) adjust an existing structure to meet a temperature target, (2) use two structures to blend water to meet a temperature target, and (3) print out temperature volumes in the reservoir at specified temperatures.

docs.title: Output Frequency
docs.text:
Selective input control file
Temperature outlet control - frequency of output for temperature
OUT FREQ TFRQTMP
        0.02083

TFRQTMP (Real F8.0) is the Julian day frequency of the output for the temperature of each structure outlet. The value must be in columns 9-16 in Fortran F fixed format. A value of 0.02083 Julian day corresponds to every 30 minutes.

docs.title: Dynstr1 Card
docs.text:
DYNSTR1  CONTROL    NUM    FREQ
             ON       2    0.50
Variable Format Description CONTROL Character A8 ON or OFF: controls whether the algorithm is used NUM Integer I8 Number of selective withdrawal structures. Each subsequent line defines one structure FREQ Real F8.0 Julian day frequency for checking the temperature criteria. Set to 1.0 to check daily, 0.5 for every 12 hours

docs.title: Dynstr2 Card
docs.text:
DYNSTR2  ST/WD    JB  JS/NW  YEARLY   TSTR   TEND   TEMP  NELEV  ELEV1  ELEV2
1           ST     1      1      ON   010.   045.   15.0      2  210.   190.
2           ST     2      1      ON   180.   300.   20.0      1   95.0
Variable Format Description ST/WD Character A8 ST for a structure, WD for a withdrawal JB Integer I8 Branch number of the structure. Ignored for a withdrawal JS/NW Integer I8 Outlet number (if ST/WD='ST') or withdrawal number (if ST/WD='WD') YEARLY Character A8 ON or OFF. If ON, Julian days TSTR and TEND are applied yearly (must be 1--366). If OFF, applied only once TSTR Real F8.0 Beginning Julian day for starting selective withdrawal TEND Real F8.0 Ending Julian day for ending selective withdrawal. After TEND, the outlet elevation reverts to the control file value TEMP Real F8.0 Temperature criterion in °C for lowering or raising the structure elevation NELEV Integer I8 Number of selective withdrawal elevations (up to 100) ELEV1, ELEV2, ... Real Elevations in m of the selective withdrawal structures, ordered from high to low

The model raises the elevation if the temperature criterion TEMP is above the actual temperature, or lowers the elevation if the actual temperature is above TEMP.

docs.title: Monitor Card
docs.text:
MONITOR LOC ISEG    ELEV  DYNSEL
1            32        0     OFF
2            43        1     OFF
Variable Format Description ISEG Integer I8 Segment number for temperature monitoring. If < 0, the absolute value must equal the withdrawal number segment in the WITH OUT card, and all withdrawals at that segment are combined. If = 0, uses the mixed outlet temperature of the structure/withdrawal. If > 0, uses the segment number as the monitoring point ELEV Real F8.0 Elevation for temperature monitoring. A negative number indicates a layer number. If ISEG=0 or ISEG<0, this is ignored DYNSEL Character A8 ON or OFF. If ON, a time-varying temperature criterion file named dynselectiveX.npt (where X is the structure number) is read

When DYNSEL is ON, the time-varying temperature file has the following format:

Dynamic selective input temperature input file 'dynselective1.npt'

    JDAY    TEMP
   1.000    10.0
  50.000    12.0
 150.000    15.0
 200.000    20.0
 265.000    15.0
 365.000    10.0

This time series is treated as a step function input with no linear interpolation between successive values. If the file begins with a $ character, it is read as comma-delimited CSV format.

docs.title: Auto Elevcontrol Card
docs.text:
AUTO ELEVCONTROL
1              ON
2             OFF

ELEVCONTROL (Character A8) is either ON or OFF. When ON, the elevation of the selective withdrawal structure is reduced as the water level lowers, ensuring the water surface is always above the outlet elevation. This card is repeated for each outlet (number defined by NUM in the DYNSTR1 card).

docs.title: Split1 Card
docs.text:
SPLIT1    CNTR     NUM
            ON       1
Variable Format Description CNTR Character A8 ON or OFF: activates the flow-splitting algorithm NUM Integer I8 Number of outlet pairs to consider. Outlets must be from the same branch and defined in the control file

docs.title: Split2 Card
docs.text:
SPLIT2  ST/WD    JB  YEARLY   TSTR   TEND  TTARGET  NOUTS JS1/NW1 JS2/NW2  ELCONT DYNSPLT
1          ST     2      ON   010.   045.     12.       2       2       3     OFF      ON
Variable Format Description ST/WD Character A8 ST for a structure, WD for a withdrawal JB Integer I8 Branch number. Ignored for a withdrawal YEARLY Character A8 ON or OFF: apply TSTR and TEND yearly TSTR Real F8.0 Beginning Julian day for flow splitting TEND Real F8.0 Ending Julian day for flow splitting TTARGET Real F8.0 Temperature target (°C) at the branch outlet centerline NOUTS Integer I8 Number of outlets to apportion flows (current limit is 2) JS1/NW1 Integer I8 Structure or withdrawal number for the upper outlet JS2/NW2 Integer I8 Structure or withdrawal number for the lower outlet ELCONT Character A8 ON or OFF. If ON, the top outlet elevation follows the water surface when it drops below the outlet centerline DYNSPLT Character A8 ON or OFF. If ON, a time-varying temperature target file (dynselectiveX_splt.npt) is used instead of TTARGET

The decision rules for apportioning flows between two outlets are:

Rule Condition 1 If T_JS1 > T_target and T_JS2 > T_target, take all flow from lower outlet (JS2) 2 If T_JS1 < T_target and T_JS2 < T_target, take all flow from upper outlet (JS1) 3 If T_JS1 > T_target and T_JS2 < T_target, apportion flow based on flow balance equation: Q_JS1 = Q_sum(T_target - T_JS2) / (T_JS1 - T_JS2) and Q_JS2 = Q_sum - Q_JS1 4 If water elevation is below outlet elevation for upper outlet (JS1), take all flow from lower outlet (JS2)

docs.title: Thresh1 and Thresh2 Cards
docs.text:
THRESH1  TEMPN
             2

THRESH2  TCRTWB1  TCRTWB2  TCRTWB3  TCRTWB4  TCRTWB5
1           10.0     10.0                                ! 52 deg. F
2           12.5     12.5                                ! 60 deg. F
Variable Format Description TEMPN Integer I8 Number of temperature criteria for each waterbody TCRTWBx Real F8.0 Temperature threshold (°C) for each waterbody. The model outputs the volume of the reservoir at or below each threshold

docs.title: SELECTC = USGS
docs.text:
When SELECTC='USGS', the input file is also named w2_selective.npt but has a different format supporting the USGS blending algorithm. This algorithm supports up to 10 outlets in a blending group. See Rounds and Buccola (2015) for details on the algorithm and example problems.

Two new variables were added to the SPLIT1 input card:

Variable Description TSFREQ Frequency (fraction of a day) at which blending calculations are updated TSCONV Convergence criterion for the iterative blending solution (fraction of total flow assigned to first-priority outlets; should be 0.1 or less, default 0.005)

Additional input cards for the USGS algorithm include:

Card Variable(s) Description SPLIT2 TSDYN ON or OFF: use time-varying temperature targets from dynsplit_selectiveX.npt SPLIT2 TSSHARE ON or OFF: share releases among set-2 outlets (ON) or choose the best single outlet (OFF) SPLITOUT JS1/NW1...JS10/NW10 Structure or outlet numbers (up to 10) DEPTH DEPTH1...DEPTH10 Nonzero value makes outlet a floating outlet at that depth below the water surface MINFRAC MINFRC1...MINFRC10 Minimum flow fraction (0--1) for each outlet. Negative values are interpreted as minimum flow rates in m³/s PRIORITY PRIOR1...PRIOR10 Integer priority setting. A value of -1 means the outlet is not blended but its temperature effect is accounted for. Values of 0 or greater are blending priorities (lower values = higher priority) MINHEAD MINHD1...MINHD10 Minimum head (depth in m) required for the outlet to be used MAXHEAD MAXHD1...MAXHD10 Maximum head (depth in m). If centerline is deeper than this, the outlet is not used MAXFLOW MAXFLO1...MAXFLO10 Maximum flow in m³/s for each blended outlet

Example w2_selective.npt file for SELECTC='USGS':

Figure 36. Example of possible configurations with the USGS algorithm (Rounds and Buccola, 2015).

Error Trapping

Error trapping for the USGS blending routine checks the following conditions:

  • At least 2 and no more than 10 outlets must be specified for NOUTS in each blending group on the SPLIT2 input card
  • Any single outlet can only be specified once in each blending group (SPLITOUT input card)
  • Any single outlet can only be specified in one blending group or temperature control device at a time (start and end dates for each group are checked)
  • Integer priority specifications must be -1 or greater (PRIORITY input card)

docs.title: Environmental Performance Criteria
docs.text:
This section describes the environmental performance criteria input file, which allows the model user to assess model predictions of state variables and how they can be affected by management changes. The model reads the file w2_envirprf.npt if the ENVIRPC control is set to ON in the control file (w2_con.npt or w2_con.csv).

The analysis computes a histogram of the fraction of time and volume during a model run where the selected water quality state variable falls between specified intervals. This input file allows the model user to:

  1. Compute fraction of the reservoir volume and time associated with velocity, temperature, and depth levels
  2. Compute fraction of the reservoir volume and time associated with model state variables for water quality
  3. Compute fraction of the reservoir volume and time associated with model-derived variables for water quality

The analysis produces the following output files (when all options are turned on):

Output File Contents envrprf_t.csv Temperature histogram envrprf_v.csv Velocity histogram envrprf_depth.csv Depth histogram envrprf_c.csv Concentration histogram for state variables envrprf_cd.csv Concentration histogram for derived variables

The input file w2_envirprf.npt is CSV (comma delimited) or fixed format. The model checks the file to determine which format is being used.

docs.title: File Format
docs.text:
ENVIRONMENTAL PERFORMANCE CRITERIA CE-QUAL-W2 MODEL
IINTVLS  INTVLS SELECTC   JDAY1   JDAY2   ISTR1   IEND1   ISTR2   IEND2
1            20     OFF   100.    150.        5      25

docs.title: Header and Interval Settings
docs.text:
The first two lines are ignored and serve as titles.

Variable Format Description IINTVLS Integer I1 Number of segment intervals for computing histograms (1--9). Setting this to 1 uses all active segments. Each additional interval requires an ISTR and IEND pair INTVLS Integer I8 Number of intervals (bins) for the output histogram SELECTC Character A3 ON or OFF. If OFF, all days and all active model cells are used. If ON, JDAY1, JDAY2, ISTR1, and IEND1 define the range JDAY1 Real F8.0 Start Julian day for the analysis. Use negative values for multi-year runs (e.g., -213 for August start every year) JDAY2 Real F8.0 End Julian day for the analysis ISTR1 Integer I8 First segment number for the analysis IEND1 Integer I8 Last segment number for the analysis ISTR2, IEND2 Integer I8 Additional segment interval pairs (up to 9 intervals)

docs.title: Velocity, Temperature, and Depth Settings
docs.text:
VELOCTY   VINCR   VTOP   TEMPC   TINCR   TTOP  DEPTHC   DINCR   DTOP
    OFF   0.050   0.50      ON     1.0   30.0     OFF     4.0   110.0
Variable Format Description VELOCTY Character A8 ON or OFF: compute a histogram of velocities VINCR Real F8.0 Velocity increment in m/s VTOP Real F8.0 Maximum velocity in the histogram TEMPC Character A8 ON or OFF: compute a histogram of temperatures TINCR Real F8.0 Temperature increment in °C for histogram bins TTOP Real F8.0 Maximum temperature in °C for the histogram output DEPTHC Character A8 ON or OFF: compute a histogram of depths in m DINCR Real F8.0 Depth increment in m for histogram bins DTOP Real F8.0 Maximum depth in m for the histogram output

docs.title: Constituent State Variables
docs.text:
CST       ACTIVE INTSCLE TOPLMIT
TDS          OFF   1.00   20.00
WaterAge      ON   1.00   20.00
Gen2          ON   1.00   20.00
GEN3          ON   1.00   20.00
ISS1          ON   1.00   20.00
PO4          OFF   1.00   20.00
NH4          OFF   1.00   20.00
...
DO            ON   0.50   10.00         ! 26
...

Each constituent state variable has the following fields:

Variable Format Description ACTIVE Character A8 ON or OFF: include this constituent in the histogram analysis INTSCLE Real F8.0 Interval scale (increment) for histogram bins. For DO, a value of 0.5 gives 0.5 mg/L bins TOPLMIT Real F8.0 Maximum value for the histogram. For DO with INTSCLE=0.5 and TOPLMIT=10.0, there are 20 bins

The constituent list follows the standard CE-QUAL-W2 constituent order. The ! character can be used for inline comments.

docs.title: Derived Variables
docs.text:
CST DERI  ACTIVE INTSCLE TOPLMIT
DOC          OFF   1.00   20.00
POC          OFF   1.00   20.00
TOC          OFF   1.00   20.00
DON          OFF   1.00   20.00
...
SECCHI       OFF   1.00   20.00

The derived variables section has the same format as the state variables section. Derived variables include DOC, POC, TOC, DON, PON, TON, TKN, TN, DOP, POP, TOP, TP, APR, CHLA, ATOT, %DO, TDG, Turbidity, TSS, TISS, CBOD, pH, CO₂, HCO₃, CO₃, and SECCHI.

Setting Up Environmental Performance Criteria

When setting up the environmental performance criteria, focus on constituents that are relevant to your management questions. Turn ACTIVE to ON only for variables of interest to minimize output file sizes. Adjust INTSCLE and TOPLMIT to provide appropriate histogram resolution for each variable.

The typical output file is comma delimited and can be opened directly in Excel. The first series of output lines form a histogram of the fraction of volume and time that the variable was in the specified interval. At the end of the column there is a sum of the fractions (which should sum to 1.0) and the last line is the temporal and volume-weighted average over the entire model domain and simulation time period.

docs.title: Snapshot File
docs.text:
The snapshot file was designed for output to a hard copy printer and contains useful information that can be utilized during model application. The file can be read using any text editor. It is not recommended for graphing; other output files are more suitable for plotting model predictions.

The snapshot file is controlled by the SNP PRINT, SNP DATE, SNP FREQ, and SNP SEG cards. The output is updated to the file based on the update dates [SNPD] and frequency [SNPF] specified in the control file. The file contains the following sections for each output time.

docs.title: Title Cards
docs.text:
The first lines of output contain the information specified in the Title Card for identifying the run plus the date and time that the run occurred. This information will appear every time output is updated to the file. Following the title cards is information related to the progress of the run including the output date and timestep information.

Example:

CE-QUAL-W2  V3.1
 Burnsville Reservoir - March 15 through December 11, 1992
 Density placed inflow, point sink outflows
 Default hydraulic coefficients
 Default light absorption/extinction coefficients
 Default kinetic coefficients
 Temperature and water quality simulation
 Run 8
 Testing sensitivity to wind
 Wind sheltering set to 0.75
 Jim Stiles and Vince Marchese, USACE Huntington District
 Model run at 16:58:03 on 07/22/02

docs.title: Time Parameters
docs.text:
Field Variable Description Gregorian date GDAY Calendar date Julian date JDAY Julian day and hours Elapsed time ELTMJD Days and hours since simulation start Timestep DLT Current timestep (s) and location (KLOC, ILOC) Minimum timestep MINDLT Minimum timestep to date (s), date, and location Average timestep DLTAV Average timestep (s) Number of iterations NIT Total iterations to date Number of violations NV Number of timestep violations

Example:

Time Parameters
  Gregorian date     [GDAY] =                March 15, 1992
  Julian date        [JDAY] =       75 days 12.00 hours
  Timestep            [DLT] =          356 sec
    at location  [KLOC,ILOC] = (26,47)
  Average timestep  [DLTAV] =          600 sec
  Number of iterations [NIT] =           72
  Number of violations  [NV] =            5

docs.title: Meteorological Parameters
docs.text:
The next information includes meteorological parameters used at the current timestep. This can be useful when trying to understand temperature simulations. Running sensitivity analyses on meteorological forcing can show that the model will reproduce observed data if the forcing values are more accurate.

Example:

Meteorological Parameters
  Input
    Air temperature        [TAIR]  =      0.55 °C
    Dewpoint temperature   [TDEW]  =     -8.59 °C
    Wind direction          [PHI]  =      4.65 rad
    Cloud cover           [CLOUD]  =      4.53
  Calculated
    Equilibrium temperature  [ET]  =      0.00 °C
    Surface heat exchange  [CSHE]  = 0.00E+00 m/sec
    Short wave radiation    [SRO]  = 0.14E-03 °C m/sec

docs.title: Selective Withdrawal and Inflow/Outflow Parameters
docs.text: Inflows, inflow placement, and inflow temperatures are output to provide information about what the model is seeing at all inflow boundaries during the current timestep. All outflows are also printed including individual structure outflows, the layer-by-layer outflow computed from the selective withdrawal algorithm, and the total outflow. The final information includes inflow constituent concentrations for all boundary inflows.

docs.title: Balances
docs.text:
Water balance, energy balance, and mass balance results for each branch and waterbody, including:

  • Spatial and temporal change in volume/energy/mass
  • Error and percent error between the two

Balance Checks

Volume and mass balance errors should be on the order of 10⁻⁶ to 10⁻¹³ percent. Larger errors may indicate code issues or numerical instability.

docs.title: Geometry
docs.text: The water surface layer number, elevation at the downstream segment, and the current upstream segment number for each branch are output.

docs.title: Water Surface
docs.text: The water surface elevation and the water surface deviation from the top of the water surface layer number are output next. The water surface deviation uses the oceanographic convention in which the deviation downwards from the top of the surface layer is positive. The output includes information only for the segments specified on the Snapshot Segments card.

docs.title: Temperature/Water Quality
docs.text: The last information available from the snapshot file covers hydrodynamics and water quality. The user controls which variables are included in the output. Include only variables of interest since the file can become quite large. Title cards are printed on each new page for ease in identifying the simulation.

docs.title: Sediment Diagenesis Output Files
docs.text:
Output files from the sediment diagenesis routine are CSV files for graphing. Key output files include:

File Description DiagenesisLogFile.opt Layer addition information for bed consolidation DiagBubbleReleaseSummary.csv Summary of bubble release predictions DiagBubbles.csv Bubble radius, gas concentrations, crack status Diagenesis_SD_JCH4.csv Dissolved methane sediment fluxes Diagenesis_SD_JNH4.csv Sediment N flux Diagenesis_SD_JNO3.csv Sediment NO₃ flux Diagenesis_SD_JPO4.csv Sediment PO₄ flux Diagenesis_SOD.csv Sediment oxygen demand (CSOD+NCSOD) Diagenesis_NSOD.csv Nitrogenous SOD Diagenesis_CSOD.csv Carbonaceous SOD Diagenesis_JC.csv Sediment C flux from water column Diagenesis_JN.csv Sediment N flux from water column Diagenesis_JP.csv Sediment P flux from water column Diagenesis_TemperatureAerobicLayer.csv Temperature in aerobic layer Diagenesis_TemperatureAnaerobicLayer.csv Temperature in anaerobic layer Diagenesis_POCG1.csv Labile POC concentrations Diagenesis_POCG2.csv Refractory POC concentrations Diagenesis_PONG1.csv Labile PON concentrations Diagenesis_PONG2.csv Refractory PON concentrations Diagenesis_POPG1.csv Labile POP concentrations Diagenesis_POPG2.csv Refractory POP concentrations

Additional output files include porewater concentrations (NO₃, NH₃, PO₄, SO₄, Fe, Mn, CH₄ for aerobic and anaerobic layers), transfer velocities, and bubble model outputs.

docs.title: Time Series
docs.text:
A time series history can be output for any number of cells in the computational grid with output for each cell written to a separate file. Output is suitable for import into a spreadsheet program for analysis and plotting and is in comma-delimited format. If the TSR filename is set to a file suffix csv, then all TSR files will have that suffix and will open in Excel automatically. The model takes the name of the time series file specified on the TIME SERIES PLOT FILENAME card and appends _x to the filename where x = 1, 2, 3, etc., depending upon whether the cell is the first, second, third, etc. one specified on the TIME SERIES SEGMENT card.

The time series file includes the following information:

  • Julian date and current time step (s)
  • Water surface elevation for the cell's segment location (m)
  • Temperature (°C) at the layer and segment specified
  • Velocity (m s⁻¹) at the layer and segment specified
  • Total flow rate through the entire segment (m³ s⁻¹), vertically integrated flow through the segment
  • Net short wave solar radiation incident on the water surface (W m⁻²; reflection is not included, hence it would be the internally computed SRO which includes reflection x 1.06)
  • Light extinction coefficient in m⁻¹ at the layer and segment specified
  • Depth from water surface to channel bottom (m)
  • Surface width (m)
  • Shade (shade factor multiplied by SRON; if SHADE = 1, no shade; if SHADE = 0, no short wave solar reaches the water surface)
  • Net radiation at surface of segment (W m⁻²), short wave solar net at surface (W m⁻²), long wave radiation net in at surface (W m⁻²), back radiation at surface (W m⁻²), evaporative heat flux at surface (W m⁻²), conductive heat flux at surface (W m⁻²)
  • Reaeration coefficient (day⁻¹) predicted by the model at the segment of the TSR file
  • Active constituent concentrations
  • Derived constituent concentrations
  • Instantaneous kinetic flux rates in kg day⁻¹
  • Instantaneous algal growth rate limitation fractions for P, N, and light [0 to 1] for each algal group
  • If LIMC is turned on under the CST COMP card, instantaneous epiphyton growth rate limitation fractions for P, N, and light [0 to 1] for each epiphyton group

If the first-order sediment model is ON, the TSR file will also output SED (total organic matter in sediments in g m⁻³), SEDN (Organic N in sediments in g m⁻³), SEDP (organic P in sediments in g m⁻³), and SEDC (organic C in sediments in g m⁻³). The mass of organic matter, N, P, and C is normalized by the volume of the model cell in contact with the sediment layer.

Equilibrium Temperature Approach

If SLHTC is set to ET for equilibrium temperature approach, then the radiation fluxes will all be set to zero.

docs.title: Auto-Port Selection Output Files
docs.text: The auto-port selection routine writes two types of output files.

docs.title: Volume at Specified Temperatures (Volume_wbX.opt)
docs.text:
The volume at specified temperature files are named Volume_wbX.opt, where X is the waterbody number. Each file contains a time series of Julian day, total volume (m³), and volumes below the temperature thresholds defined by TEMPCRIT in the w2_selective.npt control file. The number of volume columns corresponds to the number of temperature thresholds specified.

jday     Volume       Volcrit       Volcrit
22919.05 0.1650E+10  0.1565E+10  0.1650E+10
22919.09 0.1650E+10  0.1563E+10  0.1650E+10
22919.13 0.1650E+10  0.1561E+10  0.1650E+10
22919.17 0.1650E+10  0.1560E+10  0.1650E+10
22919.21 0.1650E+10  0.1557E+10  0.1650E+10

docs.title: Outlet Temperatures and Elevations (wd_out.opt and str_brX.csv)
docs.text:
When SELECTC = ON, the model prints a separate time series of outlet temperatures and flows for each individual outlet, in addition to the existing CE-QUAL-W2 combined temperature time series. The outlet files are named str_brX.csv where X is the branch number. A similar file is written for withdrawals in wd_out.opt.

The format includes columns for Julian day, temperature for each structure, flow for each structure, and elevation for each structure.

docs.title: Fish Habitat Output Files
docs.text: There are several output files defined in the fish habitat input file: one for fish habitat, volume-weighted averages for an entire segment over all vertical layers, surface-weighted averages over a fixed number of vertical layers, and accumulation of sediments in the first-order sediment model.

docs.title: Fish Habitat
docs.text:
The fish habitat zones are defined in the w2_habitat.npt input file. The output file reprints the original criteria and then, at the output frequency of the TSR FREQ card, outputs Julian day, percent habitat volume for species 1, actual habitat volume in m³ for species 1, and then repeats this for each species.

Fish habitat analysis: CE-QUAL-W2 model results

 Species, Temperature minimum, Temperature maximum, Dissolved oxygen minimum

StripedBass,             10.00,   24.00,    5.00
Walleye,                 12.00,   24.00,    5.00
WhiteBass,                0.00,   28.00,    3.00
SmallmouthBass,           0.00,   29.00,    4.00
SpottedBass,              0.00,   24.40,    6.00

JDAY,%VOL-RainbowTrout,HAB-VOL(m3)-RainbowTrout,%VOL-StripedBass,...
   61.532,   100.00,  0.1170E+09,     0.00,  0.0000E+00,...

The model also writes output for each branch and waterbody if HABTATC is ON. For each waterbody, the model writes fish_habitat_wbX.csv where X is the waterbody number. For each branch, the model writes fish_habitat_brX.csv where X is the branch number. These files allow the model user to explore fish habitat in smaller sections of the waterbody.

docs.title: Volume-Weighted and Surface-Weighted Averages
docs.text:
Volume-weighted averages are computed at specified segments. The output includes Julian day and the following parameters at each specified segment: PO₄, NH₄, NO₃, DO, TP, Chl-a, and Gamma (an index variable).

Surface-weighted averages are similar but computed over a specified number of layers from the water surface. The format matches the fish habitat output file, with blank lines at the beginning.

docs.title: Organic Matter Accumulation
docs.text: The organic matter accumulation output file contains comma-delimited entries for each segment and time of output. The values are grams of organic matter at the bottom of each layer, summed for each segment.

docs.title: Preprocessor
docs.text:
The preprocessor produces several output files: a file that echoes all control file inputs along with additional information (pre.opt), a warning file that alerts the user to potential problems with inputs (pre.wrn), and an error file (pre.err) that identifies serious problems in the input data that may prevent the model from running or running correctly. Run the preprocessor routinely before a model simulation.

In the Windows version, the user can supply a command-line working directory argument so that the preprocessor executable does not need to be copied into every model directory:

preW2_ivf.exe "C:\scott\w2workshop\2009 workshop\waterqual\problem3"

docs.title: Output (pre.opt)
docs.text:
The title cards are echoed at the beginning of the output followed by a complete echoing of all control file input. A description of the input, the Fortran variable name used in the control file, and the value of the variable are output. The sequence of output closely follows the sequence of input in the control file, but in some cases it is different as certain types of output are more logically grouped together. The pre.opt file contains the following major sections:

Time Control and Simulation Parameters. The first section includes variables affecting the time of simulation and the timestep, followed by initial conditions and variables that control calculations in the model.

Time Control
  Starting time (Julian day) [TMSTRT] =   75.00
  Ending time (Julian day)   [TMEND]  =  320.00
  Year                       [YEAR]   =   1992
  # Timestep intervals       [NDLT]   =      1
  Minimum timestep (sec)     [DLTMIN] =    1.0
  Maximum timestep (sec)     [DLTMAX] = 1800.0
  Fraction of timestep       [DLTF]   =   0.85

Input Interpolations and Meteorological Parameters. Controls for all input interpolation are output, followed by meteorological parameters and a statistical summary of all meteorological variables in the input file.

Meteorological Data Input Summary
    Parameter  Waterbody  Average Value  Maximum   Minimum
    TAIR(C)        1        26.258       37.300    16.000
    TDEW(C)        1        22.850       29.000     8.500
    WIND(m/s)      1         0.592       11.490     0.000

Transport, Hydraulic, and Ice Cover Parameters. Variables affecting the transport solution, hydraulics, and ice cover.

Output Controls. Snapshot, screen, fluxes, vector plot, profile plot, spreadsheet plot, contour plot, time series, and restart settings with their dates and frequencies.

Inflow/Outflow Information. Selective withdrawal structure information, tributary details, withdrawal details, distributed tributary settings, and all input and output filenames.

Constituent Parameters. State variable computation, initial concentration, flux, and printout settings; boundary condition constituent controls; derived variable computation controls; kinetic rate constants; stoichiometric relationships; light attenuation coefficients; half-saturation constants.

Inflow Constituent Statistics. Summary statistics (average, maximum, minimum) for inflow temperatures and constituent concentrations.

Water Balance Summary. Average and maximum total inflows and outflows for each waterbody and branch.

Geometry. All information from the control and bathymetry file along with a computed area-volume-elevation table that includes average width, depth, and theoretical hydraulic residence time. The surface layer is indicated by KT next to the layer number.

Branch 1 Volume-Area-Elevation Table

Layer  Elevation  Area        Volume      Active Cells  Average depth  Average width
       (m)        (1.0E6 m^2) (1.0E6 m^3)               (m)            (m)

 23 KT 238.36     2.413        8.844       216            3.7           122.50

Initial Conditions. Initial conditions for the water surface deviation, temperature, and constituent concentrations. Check these to ensure correctness, particularly when using vertical and/or longitudinal profile files.

docs.title: Warning Messages (pre.wrn)
docs.text:
The preprocessor does an extensive check of inputs to determine if inputs "make sense." Because the model is flexible, certain inputs are not necessarily errors but should be flagged so the user can verify their intent. When kinetic rates differ from valid ranges or a specific value that should not normally be changed, a warning message is generated.

All warning messages include a concise statement in English showing what the problem is. The Fortran variable name is also included along with its value.

Example:

Epiphyton excretion rate [EE=0.000] < 0.001 for epiphyton group 1
Oxygen to algal respiration stoichiometry [O2AR=1.400] /= 1.1 for waterbody 1
Phosphorus/organic matter stoichiometry [ORGP=0.011] /= 0.005 for waterbody 1
Water surface elevation is below bottom elevation at segment 1
Water surface elevation is below bottom elevation at segment 2

Warning Messages

The absence of warning messages does not guarantee that all inputs are correct. Not all possible input combinations can be checked. Do not assume that because there are no warnings generated there are no problems with inputs.

docs.title: Error Messages (pre.err)
docs.text:
Input errors that will prevent the model from running correctly or running at all are extensively screened and, when found, are included in the preprocessor error output file. All error messages include a concise statement in English along with the Fortran variable name and its input value.

Example:

Starting time [TMSTRT=75.000] < ending time [TMEND=-320.000]
Timestep fraction [DLTF(1)=-0.850] <= 0.0
Internal gravity wave limitation control  [CELC= on] /= " ON" or "OFF" for waterbody 1
Heat exchange solution control [SLHTC= term] /= " TERM" or " ET" for waterbody 1
Vertical advection time weighting [THETA=-0.550] < 0.0 for waterbody 1
Selective withdrawal elevation [ESTR=137.700] < the bottom active cell elevation

docs.title: Spreadsheet Profile Plot
docs.text:
The spreadsheet profile output was designed for import into a spreadsheet program for plotting vertical profiles of temperature, constituents, and derived constituents. Output consists of a comma-delimited file with the variable name, Julian date, depth below water surface, elevation, and temperature, horizontal velocity, horizontal layer flow, and/or concentrations for the output segment. Additional segments each contain a depth, elevation, and temperature/concentration column and are continued to the right. Whenever a depth or vertical layer is part of the channel bottom, a value of -99 is placed in the cell.

Constituent,Julian_day,Depth,Elevation,Seg_9,Elevation,Seg_10,Elevation,Seg_11,Elevation,
Temperature(C),  1.500,  1.549, 439.649,  6.611, 439.649,  6.658, 439.649,  6.664,
Temperature(C),  1.500,  4.073, 437.125,  6.611, 437.125,  6.658, 437.125,  6.664,
HorizontalVelocity(ms-1), 1.500, 1.549, 439.649, -0.0001, 439.649, -0.0036, 439.649, 0.0007,
HorizontalLayerFlow(m3s-1), 1.500, 1.549, 439.649, -0.0936, 439.649, -4.1658, 439.649, 0.5209,

If SPRC is set to ONV rather than ON, an additional output file is written that contains the volume-weighted temperature, water quality state, and derived variables at the locations and times specified. This file has the suffix _volw.csv and is comma delimited.

docs.title: Profile Plot
docs.text:
The profile plot output file (prf.opt) was originally developed to provide data for a plotting package called DISSPLA from Computer Associates. The longitudinal profile plot output format is described in the next section.

As in most other output files, the card titles are included for identifying the run. The first line after the titles reports:

  1. Maximum number of layers (KMX)
  2. Number of segments for which information is output (NIPRF)
  3. Total number of output dates (NDSP)
  4. Total number of constituents (NCT)
  5. Total number of derived constituents (NDC)
  6. Pointer to the profile date currently in effect (PRFDP)
  7. Waterbody surface layer (KTWB)
  8. Logical variable: T if constituents are simulated, otherwise F
  39      1      3     17     23     12      1     23 T

The next line reports the segment(s) to output [IPRF]. The next three lines report which constituents are active. Constituent and derived constituent names follow in the next 21 lines. The constituent and derived constituent numbers follow on the next line. Temperature is always considered constituent 1. The bottom active layer for each output segment is given on the next line.

Layer heights for layers 1 through KMX are output next. Initial temperatures/constituent concentrations for each segment specified in the profile segment card are then output. The first line contains the constituent abbreviation and the number of active layers. The next line(s) contain the values for a given segment.

TEMP      14
    5.50      5.50      5.50      5.40      5.40      5.50      5.40      5.30
    5.30      5.40      5.30      5.20      5.20      5.20

The next output grouping consists of temperature/constituent concentrations over time. The first line includes Julian date (JDAY), Gregorian date (GDAY), water surface layer number (KTWB), deviation of the water surface (Z) from the top of the surface layer (KT), and how many dates information has been written.

docs.title: Longitudinal Profile Plot
docs.text:
An alternative output for the profile plot is the longitudinal profile plot. This is set in the profile plot section of the control file. The output consists of files named ProfLongJDXXX.csv where XXX is the Julian day of the profile. The output consists of model segment number, water surface elevation (m), flow rate (m³ s⁻¹), temperature (°C) of the surface layer, depth (m), width (m), volume-weighted temperature of the segment (°C), and concentrations of state variables and derived variables at the surface layer. The file is comma delimited.

docs.title: Vector Plot
docs.text: The vector plot output writes a binary file that is used by the W2_POST post-processor developed by DSI, Inc. Use the filetype w2L for W2 Linkage file so that W2_Post.exe can recognize the file natively. Only the first filename for the first waterbody is used for the output for all waterbodies. The binary file contains velocity field data (horizontal and vertical velocities) at each computational cell for each output time, used to create velocity vector overlays on contour plots.

docs.title: Contour Plot
docs.text:
The contour plot output (cpl.opt) was originally included for developing DISSPLA contour plots of model output using Fortran callable subroutines. Output consists initially of time-invariant grid information:

  1. Title cards
  2. Number of branches (NBR)
  3. Grid dimensions (KMX and IMX)
  4. Branch upstream and downstream segments (US and DS)
  5. Segment length (DLX)
  6. Layer heights (H)
  7. Number of active constituents
  8. Active constituent names

During simulations, the following time-varying information is output:

  1. Julian date (JDAY) and Gregorian date (GDAY)
  2. Water surface layer (KTWB)
  3. Tributary inflows (QTR) and temperatures (TTR)
  4. Tributary inflow concentrations for each active constituent (CTR)
  5. Current upstream segment (CUS)
  6. Branch inflow (QIN) and the sum of the branch inflow (QSUM)
  7. Interfacial area (BHRKT1) for all active segments in the surface layer (KT)
  8. Interfacial area (BHR) for all remaining active computational cells
  9. Horizontal velocities (U)
  10. Flows (QC)
  11. Water surface deviations (Z)
  12. Temperatures
  13. Constituent concentrations

The user must develop their own plotting program to use this feature unless the TECPLOT option is chosen.

docs.title: TECPLOT Output
docs.text:
When the TECPLOT option is ON, the output consists of elevation (m), longitudinal distance (m), U (x-velocity, m s⁻¹), W (z-velocity, m s⁻¹), T (°C), RHO (kg m⁻³), Fish Habitat number, and concentrations for all active constituents for the entire grid at the time interval specified in CPL FREQ. Tecplot can read the file directly and the user can create contour animations of any variables including superimposed velocity vector plots.

The Fish Habitat number is the fish criterion satisfied at each grid point (K,I). Define fish criteria in order of more restrictive to least restrictive:

OptimalFishX,12.0,18.0,5.0
SuboptimalFishX,10.0,22.0,5.0
NonOptimalFishX(Lethal),0.0,35.0,4.0

The first fish is given #1, second #2, and 3rd fish group #3. For each grid point, the habitat criteria value 1, 2, 3, or 100 (if outside the last range) is written to the Tecplot output file.

To create a contour animation in Tecplot:

  1. Import data (cpl.opt) into Tecplot using the Tecplot Data Loader.
  2. Turn ON contours.
  3. Reset axes so that they are Independent (Tecplot default is dependent).
  4. Turn on Value Blanking since state variables outside the domain are set to -99.
  5. Reset the contour intervals since Tecplot automatically uses -99 as its minimum data value.
  6. Go to the animation and view the zones on screen or export to an AVI file.
  7. To add vectors, turn on vectors and choose U and W as the vector variables.

docs.title: Withdrawal Outflow
docs.text:
Whenever withdrawal output control [WDOC] is ON (see w2_con.npt or w2_con.csv file), withdrawal outflow files contain information for plotting any release or withdrawal temperatures and/or constituent concentrations as a time series. The files can also be used to externally link upstream waterbodies to downstream waterbodies so that waterbasins can be broken up into multiple waterbodies. This is an important feature when runtimes for the entire waterbasin become excessive. With this option, calibration can start at the most upstream waterbody and proceed sequentially downstream.

The model user can specify the output filenames by specifying WDOFN (see Withdrawal Output (WITH OUT) card). WDOFN can describe a subdirectory and filename. For example, if WDOFN=.\wdo files\Lake1.csv, then the output files will be written to a subdirectory called wdo files.

docs.title: Integrated Output
docs.text:
Output consists of up to four separate files for each segment [IWDO] specified in the control file:

File Type Contents q_AAA_segXX.YYY Flow rates (m³ s⁻¹) t_AAA_segXX.YYY Temperatures (°C) c_AAA_segXX.YYY Constituent concentrations d_AAA_segXX.YYY Derived constituent concentrations

Where AAA is the withdrawal output filename entered for WDOFN, XX is the segment number (IWDO), and YYY is the filetype given for the WDO output file. These files are for all the withdrawals specified at that segment lumped together if there are multiple withdrawals. The constituent concentration outflow file is only generated if constituent computations [CCC] are turned on. The derived constituent concentration outflow file is generated only if constituent computations are turned on and one or more derived constituents [CDWBC] are turned on.

For the flow and temperature files, individual flows and outlet temperatures are provided to the right of the weighted average (temperature) or summed flow. All output files are in comma-delimited format and are in the correct format for a downstream inflow or tributary file.

docs.title: Individual Output
docs.text:
A series of individual comma-delimited files are also output for each structure at the withdrawal segment. For example, if there are 2 spillways (weirs), 1 gate and 1 pump at the withdrawal segment, all these withdrawal types are automatically output individually as separate files with a fixed internally specified file name based on the hydraulic element and the segment number, such as: qwo_sp1_seg23.csv, qwo_sp2_seg23.csv, qwo_gate1_seg23.csv, and qwo_pmp1_seg23.csv. These files have only flow, temperature, and concentration for one outlet. Similarly named output files are provided for gates, spillways, and pipes if they are located at the withdrawal output segment [IWDO].

WDO Output

WDO output files are not multiplied by CMULT or CDMULT, unlike the snapshot and time series output files.

docs.title: Mass Balance Output File
docs.text:
When Mass_Balance [MBC] is turned ON (see CALCULATIONS in control file), the model outputs a summary of the N and P mass balance for each waterbody based on the output interval for CPL output with the name massbal.csv. If CPL output is turned OFF, [CPLC]=OFF, or if [MBC] is OFF or if no derived variables were turned ON (TP, total phosphorus, and TN, total nitrogen, must be turned ON), then no file will be written. This file is useful in looking at waterbody overall N and P balances. The file includes:

  • Julian day and waterbody number
  • Total phosphorus and total nitrogen in water column (kg), sediments (kg), and plants (kg)
  • Cumulative TP and TN in outflow, tributaries, distributed tributaries, withdrawals, precipitation, and inflow (kg)
  • Cumulative sediment release and flux to sediments (kg)
  • Sediment diagenesis flux terms (kg)

docs.title: Flow Balance Output File
docs.text:
When Volume_Balance [VBC] is ON (see CALCULATIONS in control file), the model outputs a summary of the flow balance for each waterbody based on the output interval for Contour output or CPL output in a file named flowbalance.csv. If CPL output is turned OFF, [CPLC]=OFF, or Volume_Balance [VBC] is OFF, then no file will be written. This output file is useful in looking at waterbody overall flows. The output file consists of the following information:

  • Julian day and waterbody number
  • Inflow volume to waterbody from Qin files in m³
  • Inflow volume from precipitation in m³
  • Outflow volume from outlet structures in m³
  • Output volume from withdrawals in m³
  • Output volume from evaporation in m³
  • Input volume from distributed tributaries in m³
  • Input volume from tributaries in m³
  • Volume of ice formation/ice melting in m³ (this is zero if [ICEC] is OFF)
  • Percent error in computing the fluid mass balance

The volumes and percent error between Julian days are cumulative, not instantaneous, and are negative for an outflow and positive for an inflow. Note that if one has ice formation removing water and later ice melting back into the waterbody, there should not be any net gain or loss of water.

docs.title: SYSTDG Output File
docs.text:
TDG (Total Dissolved Gas) concentrations computed with the SYSTDG equations are written into the withdrawal output files. Withdrawal outflow files contain information with release or withdrawal TDG concentrations in the time series output files. The model output consists of up to four separate files for the individual segment [IWDO] specified in the W2 control file. The files include an outflow, outflow temperature, constituent concentrations, and derived constituent concentrations. These files are for all the withdrawals specified at that segment lumped together if there are multiple withdrawals. All output files are in comma-delimited format. Also, whenever withdrawal output is ON, a series of individual files is also written in the output file for each structure at the withdrawal segment.

An additional TDG target output file, TDGTarget_output.opt, is generated from the model if TDGTA is turned ON. This file contains information for outflow release or spillway TDG concentrations and outflows as a time series file.

docs.title: Lake River Contour Plots Output Files
docs.text:
When the lake_river_contour.csv input file is present, the model produces output files for lake and river contour plots:

  • LakeContour_DO_SegXX.csv: Lake contour for dissolved oxygen at segment XX
  • Lake_Contour_T_SegXX.csv: Lake contour for temperature at segment XX
  • RiverContour_DO_BrYY.csv: River contour for dissolved oxygen for branch YY
  • RiverContour_T_BrYY.csv: River contour for temperature for branch YY

Two output formats are available:

  1. Format 1: Columns of JDAY, elevation (or distance), and temperature/dissolved oxygen (DO) value
  2. Format 2: Elevations (or distances) in the first row; rows are time steps with temperature/DO values at each elevation (or distance)

docs.title: Water Level Output File
docs.text:
A convenient file for plotting water level variations as a function of time and space is written out if the TIME_SERIES is ON. The output file name is wl.csv. The file consists of Julian day followed by the water surface elevation at each model segment in m. The water level at every model segment is written rather than those specified in the TIME_SERIES output. An example file is shown below:

JDAY,SEG    2,SEG    3,SEG    4,...,SEG   65,SEG
1.001,1484.700,1484.700,1484.700,...
1.150,1484.700,1484.700,...

docs.title: W2Anim Output File
docs.text:
If the user uses Stewart Rounds' W2Anim post-processor (https://github.com/sarounds/w2anim/releases/latest), one of the files used for viewing the flow, temperature, and water quality of outlets is now automatically output. This file is used for viewing the outlet dynamics (flow, temperature, and water quality) for any outflow. The output file is written whenever there is a WDO (withdrawal output) specified.

The file is internally named based on the prefix and suffix specified for the WDO output file. The file name is qwo_layers_XX_wdo.csv if the prefix was wdo and the suffix was csv, where XX is the segment number where the withdrawal occurs. The file contains:

  • Row 1: Header identifying the file as "Flow layers file for segment XX"
  • Row 2: Column headers including "Output is total outflow, WS elev, El(Kbm)" and "layer outflows starting w/ layer 2"
  • Row 3: Column labels for JDAY, Q(m3/s), El(Kbm), and LayerFlow(m3/s)
  • Subsequent rows: Time series of Julian day, total outflow, water surface elevation, bottom elevation, and flow in each layer starting with layer 2

The column D starts with the flow in layer 2, column E is the flow in layer 3, and so on.

docs.title: Run-time Warnings
docs.text:
The model generates the following run-time warning messages that can be useful when setting up the model and debugging errors that may have occurred. These are output to the file w2.wrn.

  1. Water surface is above the top of layer 2 in segment 'x' at day 'y'. This message informs the user that the water surface elevation has gone above the top of the computational grid. This may be okay or it might indicate that additional layers need to be added to the grid so that the surface layer does not become inappropriately thick. This is a common message when first calibrating the water surface in a reservoir if either the inflows are overestimated or the outflows are underestimated.

  2. Computational warning at Julian day = 'x,' at segment 'y' timestep = 'z' water surface deviation [Z] = 'x' m layer thickness = 'y' m. This message indicates that the water surface elevation solution is starting to go unstable as a result of velocities approaching supercritical values. The water surface elevation has gone from residing in layer KT to layer KT+1, which causes a negative surface layer thickness. The surface layer thickness, HKT1, is the layer thickness, H, minus the water surface deviation, z, from the top layer KT. This is negative when the solution begins to go unstable.

    Normally, when the water surface elevation approaches the bottom of layer KT, the model would subtract a layer thus allowing the water surface level to decline smoothly over time. However, if the water surface elevation jumps below the bottom of layer KT in one timestep, the layer subtraction algorithm does not have a chance to adjust the water surface layer before solving for the velocities.

  3. Unstable water surface elevation on day 'x,' negative surface layer thickness using minimum timestep at iteration 'y'. The model attempts to recover from the instability by decreasing the timestep by 90% and recomputing the water surface elevation. If the current timestep is greater than the minimum timestep [DLTMIN], then this warning message is generated. If the current timestep is less than or equal to [DLTMIN], then an error message is output and the run is stopped. To recover, reduce [DLTMAX] and/or [DLTF] just prior to the instability and then increase back to original values later in the simulation.

  4. Low water in segment 'x' water surface deviation ='y' at day 'z'. This warning message alerts the user that water is drying up in a segment with only one active layer. This may mean that more friction is required to hold back water in downstream segments or the segment in question, or that segments upstream may need to have less friction.

  5. Computational warning at Julian day = 'x' spatial change ='x' m³ temporal change ='y' m³ volume error ='z' m³. This message lets the user know that the volume error is more than 1000 m³. This should not normally happen unless the user has incorrectly modified the code or the water surface elevation solution has become unstable.

  6. Change of model surface layer by adding or subtracting layers. Informational diagnostic message.

  7. Other diagnostic information.

Instability Recovery

If the instability is occurring during high inflow periods, the user can spread inflows out over a greater time period to reduce maximum velocities. Care must be taken to ensure that the total inflows remain the same, especially if inflow interpolation [QINIC] is turned on. Velocities can also be reduced through adjustments to the bathymetry such as making cells wider. If inflows are placed according to density [PQINC] and/or [PQTRC], velocities can also be reduced by using the "distribute evenly from top to bottom" option. Another option is to increase the minimum number of layers [NLMIN] for a segment to remain active.

docs.title: Run-time Errors
docs.text: When the model goes unstable and stops running, the code generates two files: w2.err and w2errordump.csv. The model generates the run-time error messages and outputs them to w2.err, and generates an error "dump" file of all the pertinent output at the time of the model crash, w2errordump.csv. Both of these files are useful in debugging the cause of a model instability and "crash."

docs.title: W2.err
docs.text:
Error 1: Unstable water surface elevation on day 'x' negative surface layer thickness using minimum timestep at iteration 'y'

As discussed in the Run-time Warnings section, this error message is generated by an unstable water surface elevation solution. Additional information output to the error file includes the segment number, the water surface elevation at that segment, the bottom elevation of that segment, and the elevation difference for all segments in the offending branch.

The model user may need to lower DLTMAX forcing the model to run at a lower time step around the period of instability. Or perhaps the model is drying up, and there is insufficient water in the main branch. This involves reassessing the inflows and outflows to your waterbody. Examine all preprocessor warnings in case there were no errors and check each one to see if that is a cause of the problem.

Error 2: Fatal error: Insufficient segments in branch 'x' Julian day = 'y' water surface layer = 'z'

Currently in the model, if the number of segments in the main branch becomes less than two due to drying out and subsequent subtraction of upstream segments from the active computational grid, then the model issues this error message and terminates. There must be at least two active segments in the main branch for many of the computations to proceed. This error is most common in reservoir simulations. For all side-branches off the mainstem branch, a branch can go inactive if it dries up.

If this occurs during water surface calibration due to insufficient inflows or excessive outflows, then adjust the flows so that either more water comes in or less water flows out. Another workaround is to add additional depth to the bottom of the branch so that water levels can drop without segments being subtracted. Similarly, the number of active layers required to prevent segment subtraction [NLMIN] can be set to one if it is not already set to that value.

Example:

negative surface layer thickness using minimum timestep at iteration 295

docs.title: W2ErrorDump.csv
docs.text:
This file provides comprehensive diagnostic information at the time of model crash. The variable names shown in the dump file are as follows:

Variable Description JDAY Julian day at time of model crash QIN Inflow flow rates in m³ s⁻¹ for each model branch QTR Tributary inflow flow rates in m³ s⁻¹ for each tributary QDT Distributed inflow flow rates in m³ s⁻¹ for each branch QWD Withdrawal flow rates in m³ s⁻¹ for each withdrawal SEG Segment number (I) BRANCH Branch number KT Surface layer WSE Water surface elevation in m SZ Prior time step deviation of the surface layer water surface from KT Z Current time step deviation of the surface layer water surface from KT Q Flow rate between model segments computed from horizontal momentum equation QC Corrected flow rate between model segments computed from continuity balance (this is what is used in the model) QERR Differences in flow rate between Q and QC H2KT Prior time step surface layer depth H1KT Current time step surface layer depth BHR1 Current time step right hand side area (depth times width) of the surface layer BHR2 Prior time step right hand side area (depth times width) of the surface layer T1 Current time step model temperature at the surface layer T2 Prior time step model temperature at the surface layer SUKT Prior time step velocity of the surface layer at the right-hand side of the segment UKT Current time step velocity of the surface layer at the right-hand side of the segment

docs.title: Using Particle Transport in CE-QUAL-W2
docs.text: There are no switches in the w2_con.npt or w2_con.csv control file to turn on particle transport. The particle transport algorithm in CE-QUAL-W2 (the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers' two-dimensional hydrodynamic and water quality model) is activated by placing the input file w2_particle.csv in the default model directory of the executable. This chapter describes the w2_particle.csv input file and the output files generated by the particle transport algorithm.

docs.title: Input File: w2_particle.csv
docs.text:
The input file w2_particle.csv must be present in the model directory for the particle transport algorithm to be activated. A template for this file is included in the Excel input file under the tab w2_particle.csv.

The file is divided into three sections:

  1. Particle control and global settings (line 3)
  2. Particle deposition definitions (one line per particle group)
  3. Histogram and monitoring location settings

Note

The first two lines of w2_particle.csv are headers and are skipped by the model. The model reads data starting at line 3. All model inputs are comma delimited.

docs.title: Section 1: Particle Control
docs.text:
The first data line (line 3) contains the global particle transport settings.

Particle Input File  S.Wells PSU based on Andy Goodwin Fish Migration Program
PART CONTROL, NSEG, #PARTICLES SEGMENT, LINE, DXTHEORY, OUTFREQ (days), LINEAR, HTST BOTTOM, HTST SIDE, IDEBUG
ON, 10, 5, ON, ON, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0
Variable Description PART CONTROL ON or OFF. Turns particle transport on or off. NSEG Number of segments where particles are added. In the example above, 10 segment entries are defined in Section 2. #PART/SEG Number of particles added per segment. In the example above, 5 particles are added per model cell. LINE Distributes particles in a line from top to bottom at a segment. When ON, the top and bottom layers are defined in Section 2 for each segment. DXTHEORY When ON, ignores the value of DX in the control file for longitudinal dispersion and uses a theoretically computed value based on the segment length: DISPX = 5.84×10⁻⁴ × DLX¹·¹, where DLX is the segment length in m and DISPX is the longitudinal dispersion coefficient in m² s⁻¹. The random movement in x is very sensitive to the value of DX. Adjusting values of DX in the control file with DXTHEORY set to OFF will affect the random component significantly. OUTFREQ Output frequency of model files in days. ILINEAR When set to 1, uses linear interpolation rather than a 3rd-order Newton interpolating polynomial for computing the velocity field for the particles. HTSTBOTTOM When set to 0, particles are reflected off the bottom upon contact. When set to 1, particles are removed from the system upon bottom contact. HTSTSIDE When set to 0, particles are reflected off the side upon contact. When set to 1, particles are removed from the system upon side contact. IDEBUG When set to 1, extensive debug information is written to the output. Set to 0 to disable.

docs.text:

Variable Description PARTSEG Segment number where particles are deposited. TOPK Top layer for particle distribution. BOTTOMK Bottom layer for particle distribution. FXLOC Distance in m from the upstream edge of the segment for particle placement. FZLOC Distance in m from the top of the cell for particle placement. Not used when particles are distributed as a LINE in each layer. SEDVEL Sedimentation velocity in m d⁻¹, for particles that are not neutrally buoyant. DATE Julian day for particle release. If this value is less than the simulation start date, the particles are released at the first time step.

Tip

When LINE is ON for particle group 1 in the example above, 5 particles are added to each layer (K) from K = 100 to K = 120 at segment 61, evenly spaced in a line. When LINE is OFF, 5 particles start at the FZLOC position of 0.0 m for each layer from 100 to 120, distributed with a spacing equal to the layer height divided by the number of particles.

docs.title: Section 3: Histogram Output and Monitoring Locations
docs.text:
This section defines the histogram output for particle time histories. A time history of the temperature, velocity, and depth is recorded for every time step and every particle released. Results are written to three output files:

  • envrprf_v_particle.csv
  • envrprf_t_particle.csv
  • envrprf_depth_particle.csv

docs.title: Number of Histogram Bins
docs.text:
The first variable is the number of histogram bins (or intervals) for each variable.

NUMCLASS OR INTERVALS
30

docs.title: Histogram Bin Parameters
docs.text:
The next section defines the histogram bins or intervals for velocity, temperature, and depth.

VINCR, VTOP, TINCR, TTOP, DINCR, DTOP
0.05, 0.5, 1, 30, 0.5, 10
Variable Description VINCR Velocity bin interval in m s⁻¹. VTOP Maximum velocity in m s⁻¹. TINCR Temperature bin interval in °C. TTOP Maximum temperature in °C. DINCR Depth bin interval in m. DTOP Maximum depth in m.

docs.title: Monitoring Locations
docs.text:
The next set of parameters defines monitoring of particles as they pass different locations.

#MONITORING LOCATIONS
2
Monitoring segments
30, 60
Monitoring x shift in m within a segment starting from upstream edge
10, 5

The number of monitoring locations specifies how many sensors are placed in the system to record when a particle passes. The monitoring segments are the segment numbers where sensors are located. The monitoring x-shift is the distance in m from the upstream edge of the segment, positioning the sensor within that segment.

docs.title: Reference System for Particles in Grid
docs.text: The location of particles in the grid is identified by segment (I) and layer (K) location as well as X, Y, and Z coordinates within each layer. These are described in Part 2 of the User Manual where the particle algorithm is discussed.

docs.title: Output Files
docs.text:
The model generates output files for viewing particle transport in Tecplot. The two primary file types are BranchX.dat and PartX.npt, where X is the branch number.

  • BranchX.dat contains branch characteristics such as velocity, temperature, and dissolved oxygen (DO).
  • PartX.npt contains the particle locations in each branch for particles currently within that branch.

docs.title: BranchX.dat
docs.text:
This file contains the following variables for each output time interval: X, Z, Water (1 if in the water, -1 if above the water surface or in the bottom), horizontal velocity (U), vertical velocity (W), temperature, dissolved oxygen (DO), layer index (KLayer), and segment index (ISegment). This file is typically used as the background layer over which particle positions are overlaid.

docs.title: Finalparticle.csv
docs.text:
This file contains the final state of all particles released in the model. The header prints out the information for each particle.

Column Description Part# Particle number Seg #I Segment number X Location within Seg from Upstream Side (m) X location within segment from upstream side Layer #K Layer number Vertical Dist from Top (m) Vertical distance from top of layer Lateral Dist from Left Bank (m) Lateral distance from left bank Branch# Branch number Particle In Model (=0) 0 if particle is still in the model JDAY left system Julian day when the particle left the system Detention Time (days) Particle detention time in days Removal Mechanism Code indicating why the particle left the system (see table below) Sed Velocity (m/d) Sedimentation velocity in m d⁻¹ Date Start Julian day when the particle was released

This file also includes additional columns of time in Julian days when the particle passed a monitoring location.

docs.title: Removal Mechanism Codes
docs.text:
The removal mechanism column indicates why the particle left the system.

Removal # Reason 1 Particle lateral removal by withdrawal 2 Particle hits bottom and sticks 3 Particle leaves at upstream external head boundary condition (BC) 4 Particle leaves at downstream external head BC 5 Particle leaves at downstream structure (dam or hydraulic structure) 6 Particle leaves by hitting side wall and sticking (left-hand side) 7 Particle leaves by hitting side wall and sticking (right-hand side)

Tip

Plot a histogram of particle detention times from the Finalparticle.csv file to evaluate residence time distributions in the system.

Figure 52. Example of particle detention time histogram using the file Finalparticle.csv. For this system the average particle detention time was 9.5 days.

docs.title: Initialparticle.csv
docs.text: This file contains the initial state of all particles added or to be added to the system. It is a valuable file for verifying that the input file w2_particle.csv was interpreted properly. The file format is the same as Finalparticle.csv described above.

docs.title: envrprf_v_particle.csv, envrprf_t_particle.csv, and envrprf_depth_particle.csv
docs.text:
These files contain histograms for each particle released in the model domain, recording velocity, temperature, and depth distributions. The file format matches that of the Environmental Performance Criteria output files. Histograms can be aggregated across all particles to summarize overall exposure conditions.

Figure 53. Example histograms of particles released for velocity and temperature for a particle release experiment.

docs.title: Using Tecplot to Plot Particle Movement
docs.text:
The basic approach is to load branch data with temperature contours and velocity vectors, then overlay the particle positions in a second frame.

  1. Load the BranchX.dat file into Tecplot as Frame 1. Set up temperature contours and velocity vectors.
  2. Create a new frame (Frame 2) overlaying Frame 1.
  3. Load the PartX.npt data into Frame 2 and activate a scatter plot.
  4. Change the scatter symbol from the default rectangle to a circle and reduce its size.
  5. Link the frame styles between Frame 1 and Frame 2.
  6. Set the background of Frame 2 to transparent.
  7. Animate particle movement by stepping through the particle zones (the temperature and velocity zones remain fixed).
  8. To export an animation, write a Tecplot script that activates Frame 1 with Zone 1, then activates Frame 2 with Zone 1, and exports the image. Loop over all zones and write the output to a video file (e.g., mp4, avi, wmv).
Figure 54. Branch temperature, velocity, and particles in Tecplot frame.

docs.title: Using Multiple Processors for a Cascade of Waterbodies
docs.text:
When a model domain includes a cascade of waterbodies, such as reservoirs in series or a river system with a cascade of reaches, CE-QUAL-W2 provides a feature to reduce overall model run time by running multiple waterbodies simultaneously on separate processor cores. This approach applies when the water level in the downstream waterbody does not influence the upstream waterbody (i.e., no backwater effects).

Figure 55. Cascade of reservoirs or multiple waterbodies.

docs.title: Simulation Options
docs.text:
There are three options for simulating a series of waterbodies, summarized in Table 65.

Table 65. Techniques for using CE-QUAL-W2 to simulate a cascade of waterbodies.

Option Description Advantages Disadvantages 1 Single system model with multiple waterbodies and one control file Entire model is under one control file (w2_con.npt or w2_con.csv); simpler to manage The time step for stability is dictated by one of the waterbodies, causing other waterbodies to run at the lowest time step. Run times may be long. 2 Separate waterbodies in separate directories; use a batch file to automatically transfer withdrawal output files from one waterbody as input to the next Each waterbody runs according to its own minimum time step, resulting in faster simulation time compared to Option 1. [DLTMAX] can be tuned for faster runs in some waterbodies. Must break the model into multiple models, one for each waterbody. Each waterbody must wait until the upper one is completed before starting. 3 Separate waterbodies in separate directories; use the input file w2_multiple_WB.npt to point downstream waterbodies to inflow from an upstream waterbody Each waterbody runs according to its own minimum time step and does not have to wait until the upper waterbody is complete before proceeding. Faster than Options 1 and 2. [DLTMAX] can be tuned for faster runs in some waterbodies. Each model typically runs on a different core of a multi-core processor. Must break the model into multiple models, one for each waterbody.

Option 3 allows the downstream model to run even before the upstream model has completed. The downstream model uses the input file w2_multiple_WB.npt to determine where to obtain the upstream inflow boundary conditions. The downstream code can accept inflow from both branch inflows and tributaries from other waterbodies.

In model tests with multiple waterbodies, speed improvements from 22--90% have been seen.

Figure 56. Concept of running multiple waterbodies simultaneously.

Warning

This approach assumes that the water level in the downstream waterbody does not influence the upstream waterbody. If backwater effects are significant, all waterbodies must be included in a single model (Option 1).

docs.title: How to Set Up a Simulation
docs.text:
Set up a simulation with multiple waterbodies in separate directories. The following steps are required:

  1. Set withdrawal output control for each upstream waterbody. Set [WDOC] to ON in the control file (w2_con.npt or w2_con.csv) and set the outlet segment as a withdrawal outflow. These outflow files contain the withdrawal flows, temperatures, and/or constituent concentrations as a time series. These files serve as input to the downstream waterbody. Set the output frequency to a short time interval, since the model writes instantaneous flows, temperatures, and concentrations rather than integrated values between output times.

  2. Configure the downstream waterbody inflow files. For the downstream waterbody, set the inflow or tributary flow rate, temperature, and concentration file names to match the withdrawal outlet file names from the upstream waterbody. Use only the filenames (not the full directory path), since CE-QUAL-W2 copies these files into the directory of the downstream waterbody. For example, if the upstream waterbody has [WDOFN] set to wdo.csv and the withdrawal output segment is 6, the upstream model writes output files: qwo_6.csv, two_6.csv, and cwo_6.csv. The downstream model then uses these names as [QINFN], [TINFN], and [CINFN] (respectively) if these are a branch inflow.

    Note

    The inflow file from the upstream model and an output file for the downstream model cannot have the same name. If necessary, change the file extension for the [WDOFN] specification (e.g., from .csv to .npt) to avoid name conflicts.

  3. Create the w2_multiple_WB.npt file. The downstream model directory must contain a file called w2_multiple_WB.npt that specifies information on running the series of waterbodies. See the Input File w2_multiple_WB.npt section below.

  4. Start the waterbody executables in sequence. Launch the upstream waterbody executable first. A dialog box for the first waterbody will appear. Then, in the downstream waterbody directory, launch the executable. Once that waterbody starts to run, launch the next downstream executable. Start each downstream waterbody executable only after the upstream model begins generating output.

  5. Clean up files before restarting. Before starting a new simulation, either delete the files from upstream waterbodies in the downstream directory, or start each waterbody sequentially with enough time for a new input file to be copied to the downstream waterbody.

Warning

Files from upstream waterbodies must either be deleted in the downstream directory prior to starting a new simulation, or each waterbody must be started sequentially with enough time for new input files to be copied to the downstream waterbody.

docs.title: Input File w2_multiple_WB.npt
docs.text:
The input file w2_multiple_WB.npt is a text file with the following format:

Multiple WB wait ON or OFF (only 2 spaces read)
ON
Number of input types to wait for (at least 1)
2
Specific inputs to wait for:  branch inflow [BR] or trib [TR], branch/trib index number,
and directory (max 240 characters)
BR, 1, ..\WB2
TR, 3, ..\WB3
Buffer time to run program, days (wait until at least XX days available)
2
Delay time in seconds to wait for buffer and recheck
60

Each header line between data lines is used for comments and is ignored by the model. The input fields are described in Table 66.

Table 66. Description of input file w2_multiple_WB.npt.

Variable Description Multiple WB wait ON or OFF ON or OFF. Turns on or off the multiple waterbody run feature. Only the first 2 characters are read. Number of input types to wait for Number of model inputs to the downstream waterbody. Must be at least 1, but can be multiple input files. Specific inputs to wait for: branch inflow [BR] or trib [TR], branch/trib index number, and directory (max 240 characters) Specifies the directory of the upstream waterbody, whether it is a branch inflow (BR) or a tributary inflow (TR), and the branch or tributary number, followed by the directory path of that file. In the example above, a relative directory path was used. ..\WB2 means to go up one directory to a subdirectory WB2. An absolute directory path can also be used. Buffer time in days How many days of output data from the upper waterbody must be available before starting the downstream waterbody computation. Delay time in seconds to wait for checking upstream boundary The time in seconds for the downstream waterbody to pause before checking to see if the buffer time is satisfied. If one chooses a 2-day buffer time, the downstream model would check at "delay time" intervals to see if the required number of output days are complete before continuing to run.

This file is also included in the Excel input file under the tab w2_multiple_WB.npt. Select the highlighted section in Excel and click the export button to write the text file.

docs.title: Output File WaitForRunLog.opt
docs.text:
An output file WaitForRunLog.opt is produced showing how the downstream model copied files from the upstream waterbody. This file is used for debugging model errors. An example of this file is shown below:

    1.0000  COPY ..\WB1\qwo_6.csv
    1.0000  COPY ..\WB1\two_6.csv
Execution stopped at    10.900 WAITING FOR RESTART
   10.9000  COPY ..\WB1\qwo_6.csv
   10.9000  COPY ..\WB1\two_6.csv
Execution stopped at    22.350 WAITING FOR RESTART
   22.3500  COPY ..\WB1\qwo_6.csv
   22.3500  COPY ..\WB1\two_6.csv
Execution stopped at    32.850 WAITING FOR RESTART
   32.8500  COPY ..\WB1\qwo_6.csv
   32.8500  COPY ..\WB1\two_6.csv
Execution stopped at    43.080 WAITING FOR RESTART
   43.0800  COPY ..\WB1\qwo_6.csv
   43.0800  COPY ..\WB1\two_6.csv
Execution stopped at    53.000 WAITING FOR RESTART
   53.0000  COPY ..\WB1\qwo_6.csv
   53.0000  COPY ..\WB1\two_6.csv

The log shows the simulation time (in Julian days) at which each file copy occurred. When the downstream model reaches the end of available input data, it displays WAITING FOR RESTART and pauses until the upstream model has produced enough additional output (as defined by the buffer time) before continuing.

Tip

Review WaitForRunLog.opt if the downstream model appears to hang or produces unexpected results. Frequent WAITING FOR RESTART messages may indicate that the buffer time is too large or the upstream model is running too slowly relative to the downstream model.

docs.title: Part 4: Model Examples
docs.text: This section of the User Manual describes the example problems distributed with the CE-QUAL-W2 model release and provides guidance on applying the model to reservoirs, estuaries, and rivers.

docs.title: Chapters
docs.text:
1. Introduction: Overview of example problems and additional resources included with the model download
  2. Model Examples Distributed with the Model Release: Descriptions of the nine example applications included in the model download package
  3. Examples of Model Applications: Calibration guidance for lakes/reservoirs, estuaries, and rivers with case studies from numerous waterbodies
  4. References: Literature cited in Part 4

docs.title: Introduction
docs.text: This part of the User Manual describes the example problems distributed with the CE-QUAL-W2 model release and provides examples of model applications to different waterbody types. It also includes updated material from the Cole and Wells (2019) User Manual, written primarily by Tom Cole, on the application of the model to reservoirs, estuaries, and rivers.
